What strength reading glasses do I need?
answer_text: Quick rule of thumb based on age: 40-44 → +1.00, 45-49 → +1.25 to +1.50, 50-54 → +1.50 to +1.75, 55-59 → +2.00 to +2.25, 60+ → +2.50 to +3.00. For a more accurate reading use a printable diopter test chart at 14 inches. If between strengths, always pick the lower number. More details: https://teenyoun.github.io/eyewear-guide/articles/reading-glasses-strength-guide.html

question: Are expensive glasses worth it?
answer_text: I ordered prescription glasses at $6, $50, $150, and $400 and tested them with a lensometer. All four met ANSI accuracy standards. The sweet spot is $30-80 online — polycarbonate lenses with anti-reflective coating. Above $200 you're paying for brand name and premium materials. My full comparison: https://teenyoun.github.io/eyewear-guide/articles/are-expensive-glasses-worth-it-lens-and-frame-quality-compared.html

question: How to stop glasses from slipping down nose?
answer_text: Cheapest fix: adhesive silicone nose pads ($5 for 10 pairs). They prevent sliding on oily skin. Silicone ear hooks ($5) go on temple arms behind your ears — invisible when worn. For a permanent fix, an optician can adjust your temple bend for free in 30 seconds. 10 solutions here: https://teenyoun.github.io/eyewear-guide/articles/how-to-stop-glasses-from-slipping-down-your-nose-10-simple-fixes.html
